sundar.48.cau1: Listen, friend: I tell you my own nature, which Kākabhuśuṇḍi, Śiva and Pārvatī know. If a man who is the enemy of all creation, moving and unmoving, comes in fear, looking to me for refuge,
sundar.48.cau2: and leaves behind pride, delusion, deceit and guile of every kind, I make him at once like a saint. Mother, father, brother, son, wife, body, wealth, house, friends and family:
sundar.48.cau3: one who gathers up the threads of attachment to all of these, twists them into a cord and with it ties his mind to my feet; who sees all with an equal eye, wants nothing at all, and whose mind holds no joy, grief or fear —
sundar.48.cau4: such a good man lives in my heart just as wealth lives in the heart of the greedy. Saints like you are dear to me; it is for no one else's sake that I take on a body.
sundar.48.do48: Those who worship the Lord with form and attributes, who are intent on the good of others and firm in right conduct and in their observances, are as my very life to me, those who love the feet of brāhmaṇas.
sundar.49.cau1: Listen, lord of Laṅkā: all these virtues are yours, and so you are exceedingly dear to me. Hearing Śrī Rāma's words, all the troops of monkeys cry: Glory to the sum of all mercy!
sundar.49.cau2: As Vibhīṣaṇa listens to the Lord's words he cannot have enough of them, knowing them to be nectar to the ears. Again and again he clasps the Lord's lotus feet; the boundless love in his heart cannot be held within it.
sundar.49.cau3: Listen, my Lord, master of all that moves and does not move, protector of those who bow before you, you who know every heart from within: at first there was some desire in my heart, but it has been carried away by the river of love for the Lord's feet.
sundar.49.cau4: Now, compassionate Lord, give me devotion to you, which makes one pure and is ever dear to Śiva's mind. The Lord, unshaken in battle, said: So be it, and at once called for water from the ocean.
sundar.49.cau5: Friend, though you have no desire, the sight of me never fails to bear fruit in this world. With these words Śrī Rāma anointed him with the tilaka, and a boundless shower of flowers fell from the sky.
sundar.49.do49क: Vibhīṣaṇa was burning in the fire of Rāvaṇa's anger, which the fierce wind of his own breath had fanned; Śrī Rāma saved him and gave him a kingdom that would never be broken.
sundar.49.do49ख: The wealth that Śiva gave Rāvaṇa when he offered up his ten heads, that same wealth Śrī Rāma gave to Vibhīṣaṇa, and gave it with diffidence.
sundar.50.cau1: Those who leave such a Lord and worship another are beasts without tail or horns. Knowing Vibhīṣaṇa for his own devotee, the Lord took him as his own; and the Lord's nature delighted the whole monkey race.
sundar.50.cau2: Then the Lord, who knows all and dwells in every heart, who is every form and yet free of all and detached, who for a purpose became a man and destroys the race of demons, spoke words that upheld right counsel:
sundar.50.cau3: Listen, heroes, king of the monkeys and lord of Laṅkā: how is this deep ocean to be crossed? It teems with crocodiles, serpents and fish of every kind; it is fathomless, and hard to cross in every way.
sundar.50.cau4: Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of Laṅkā, said: O Lord of the Raghus, listen. Your arrow could dry up ten million oceans. Even so, policy teaches that one should go to the ocean and make a humble request.
sundar.50.do50: My Lord, the Ocean is a revered elder of your line. He will think it over and tell you a way, and the entire army of bears and monkeys will get across the sea without effort.
sundar.51.cau1: Friend, the way you have told me is a good one; let it be tried, if fate is on our side. This counsel did not please Lakṣmaṇa; hearing Śrī Rāma's words, he was deeply troubled.
sundar.51.cau2: My Lord, what reliance can be placed on fate? Dry up the ocean; let your mind be roused to anger. Fate is the one prop of a coward's mind; it is the idle who keep crying out, Fate, fate.
sundar.51.cau3: On hearing this Śrī Rāma laughed and said: That is just what I shall do; keep your mind steady. With these words the Lord reassured his younger brother and went down to the ocean.
sundar.51.cau4: First he bowed his head in salutation; then he spread kuśa grass on the shore and sat down. When Vibhīṣaṇa came to the Lord, Rāvaṇa had sent spies after him.
sundar.51.do51: Disguised in the bodies of monkeys, they watched all that took place, and in their hearts they praised the virtues of the Lord and the love he bears for one who comes to him for refuge.
sundar.52.cau1: They began to praise Śrī Rāma's nature openly, and in their great love they forgot to keep up their disguise. Then the monkeys knew them for the enemy's spies, tied them all up and took them before Sugrīva, king of the monkeys.
sundar.52.cau2: Sugrīva said: Listen, all you monkeys: mutilate these demons and send them back. At Sugrīva's words the monkeys rushed at them, bound them and led them round the whole camp.
sundar.52.cau3: The monkeys began to beat them in many ways; though they cried out piteously, still the monkeys would not release them. Then they cried: Whoever cuts off our noses and ears, we charge him by the Lord of Kosala.
sundar.52.cau4: Hearing this, Lakṣmaṇa called them all to him. He was moved to pity, and with a laugh had them set free at once, and said: Put this letter into Rāvaṇa's hand and tell him: Read Lakṣmaṇa's words, you destroyer of your own race.
sundar.52.do52: And give that fool my generous message by word of mouth: Hand Sītā back and come and meet Śrī Rāma, or else your death has come.
sundar.53.cau1: At once the spies bowed their heads at Lakṣmaṇa's feet and set out, recounting a tale of virtues. Telling of Śrī Rāma's glory all the way, they came to Laṅkā and bowed their heads at Rāvaṇa's feet.
sundar.53.cau2: Rāvaṇa laughed and asked: Śuka, why don't you tell me how you are? Then give me news of Vibhīṣaṇa, whose death has drawn very near.
sundar.53.cau3: The fool gave up Laṅkā, where he lived in royal state; now the wretch will be crushed like a weevil in the barley. Then tell me about the army of bears and monkeys: cruel death has impelled it to march here.
sundar.53.cau4: That poor soft-hearted ocean has become the guardian of their lives. And then tell me about those ascetics, whose hearts are full of dread of me.
sundar.53.do53: Have you met them, or did they turn back as soon as my fair fame reached their ears? Why don't you tell me of the might and splendour of the enemy's army? Your mind seems utterly dazed.
sundar.54.cau1: My lord, as graciously as you have asked, so accept what I tell you, setting your anger aside. When your younger brother went over to them, Rāma anointed him with the tilaka the moment he arrived.
sundar.54.cau2: As soon as the monkeys heard we were spies sent by Rāvaṇa, they tied us up and made us suffer in many ways. They started cutting off our ears and noses, and only when we bound them by an oath in Rāma's name did they let us go.
sundar.54.cau3: You asked about Rāma's army, my lord: a thousand million mouths could not describe it. Its bears and monkeys are of many colours, with fearsome faces, huge and terrifying.
sundar.54.cau4: He who burned the city and killed your son has the least strength of all those monkeys. There are warriors of countless names, tough and terrible, huge and mighty, with the strength of countless elephants.
sundar.54.do54: Among them are Dvivida and Mainda, Nīla and Nala, Aṅgada and Gada, Vikaṭāsya and Dadhimukha, Kesarī, Niśaṭha and Śaṭha, and Jāmbavān, a mountain of strength.
sundar.55.cau1: All these monkeys are equal to Sugrīva, and there are millions like them; who could count so many? By Rāma's grace their strength is beyond compare; they think of the three worlds as no more than a blade of grass.
sundar.55.cau2: This I have heard with my own ears, Rāvaṇa: the monkey troop-leaders alone number eighteen padmas (a padma being an immense number). In that army, my lord, there is no monkey who would not defeat you in battle.
sundar.55.cau3: In utter fury they all wring their hands, but Rāma gives them no order. They will dry up the ocean, fish, serpents and all, or else fill it in with great mountains,
sundar.55.cau4: and crush Rāvaṇa and grind him into the dust: such are the words all the monkeys speak. Fearless by nature, they roar and threaten, as though they longed to swallow Laṅkā whole.
sundar.55.do55: The monkeys and bears are all heroes by nature, and over their heads besides is the Lord Rāma. Rāvaṇa, they could conquer ten million Deaths in battle.
sundar.56.cau1: The splendour, strength and wisdom of Rāma are so vast that a hundred thousand Śeṣas (the thousand-headed serpent) could not sing of them. He can dry up a hundred oceans with a single arrow, yet, skilled in policy as he is, he asked your brother's counsel.
sundar.56.cau2: On his advice he is asking the ocean for a way across, with mercy in his heart. Hearing this, Rāvaṇa laughed: With wits like these, no wonder he has made monkeys his allies.
sundar.56.cau3: Relying on the word of a born coward, he has taken to sulking and pestering the ocean like a spoilt child. Fool, why do you sing false praises? I have taken the measure of my enemy's strength and wit.
sundar.56.cau4: Where in the world can victory and glory be found for one whose counsellor is the timid Vibhīṣaṇa? At these words of the wicked one the spy grew angrier, and judging the moment right, he drew out the letter.
sundar.56.cau5: Rāma's younger brother gave me this letter. My lord, have it read out and let it cool your breast. Rāvaṇa laughed and took it in his left hand, and the fool called his minister and had him begin to read it.
sundar.56.do56क: Fool, do not humour your mind with mere talk and so bring your race to ruin. Opposing Śrī Rāma, you will find no escape, even if you take refuge with Viṣṇu, Brahmā and Śiva.
sundar.56.do56ख: Either give up your pride and, like your younger brother, become a bee at the Lord's lotus feet, or else, wicked one, become a moth with all your race in the flame of Śrī Rāma's arrows.
